reconcile.note: Matthew Henry proposes both evangelists abridged a fuller sermon differently, so Luke's shorter beatitude list reflects selection rather than conflicting eyewitness accounts.

discrepancy.note: Strauss notes Luke's beatitudes both omit several found in Matthew and read the shared ones in a different, more literal sense.

quotes.text: In both editions, the Sermon on the Mount is opened by a series of beatitudes; in Luke, however, not only are several wanting which we find in Matthew, but most of those common to both are in the former taken in another sense than in the latter.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), trans. George Eliot, on Matthew 5:3 and Luke 6:20.
